title: Israel strikes Khiam hours after Lebanese army deploys there
why: Mikati called it treachery by the ceasefire guarantors; first test of the 60-day withdrawal timetable.

title: Mikati tours Khiam; Israeli flag raised at Naqoura entrance
why: First Lebanese official in Khiam after withdrawal; the same day Israel kept blocking roads in the border zone.

title: Israeli forces advance into Wadi al-Hujeir, Qantara and Aadchit al-Qusayr
why: First Israeli ground advance into new areas since the ceasefire; army and UNIFIL protested.

title: Israeli drone strike kills five in Tayr Debba
why: One of the early lethal incidents under the November 2024 ceasefire, cited by CrisisWatch.

title: Constitutional Council partly annuls Law 328/2024 on suspended deadlines
why: Decision 2/2025 struck the retroactive suspension of judicial deadlines; later wartime deadline laws follow its limits.

title: Netanyahu says forces stay in south Lebanon past 26 January deadline
why: Israel declared it would not complete the 60-day withdrawal on time, leading to the 18 February extension.

title: Hezbollah and Amal supporters parade on motorbikes in Christian Beirut areas
why: Sectarian slogans and visible weapons raised civil-peace worries as the presidency changed hands.

title: Cabinet fills first top judicial posts after five years of paralysis
why: Named Abboud (Higher Judicial Council), Hajjar, Oueidat (inspection) and Youssef Gemayel (Council of State).

title: New central bank governor Souaid takes office and sets priorities
why: He told banks to recapitalise, merge or close, promised small depositors priority and an AML push toward leaving the grey list.

title: Four vacant Higher Judicial Council seats filled by decree
why: The council had been almost paralysed since October 2024; Aoun, Salam and Justice Minister Nassar co-signed.

title: Cabinet approves bank restructuring draft law; delegation at IMF-World Bank Spring Meetings
why: Finance Minister Jaber led a unified delegation; the draft became Law 23/2025 in August. Cabinet approved the draft on 12 April; the Spring Meetings delegation followed in late April.

title: Three soldiers killed as ammunition explodes in army vehicle at Braiqaa
why: Blast while moving munitions in the south; later depot blasts in August raised questions on unexploded ordnance handling.

title: Decree confirms ten Court of Cassation chamber presidents
why: Ended a three-year blockage that had frozen rulings in the port-blast and Salameh cases.

title: Law 11/2025 on non-residential leases issued
why: Parliament amended it in its 31 July 2025 session; part of the post-war economic legislation.

title: Parliament amends 2025 budget, approves World Bank solar loan, war tax relief
why: First sitting of the 2025 extraordinary session; also two supplementary credits for judges' and teachers' funds.

title: Army kills three most-wanted drug dealers in Baalbek shootout
why: Part of the Salam government's drive against drug networks in the Bekaa.

title: Iraq announces destruction of Lebanon's largest captagon plant at Yammoune
why: Result of Iraqi-Lebanese intelligence cooperation.

title: US envoy Barrack apologises after telling journalists to 'act civilised'
why: Remark at Baabda press conference caused outrage among Lebanese media.

title: Former foreign minister Abdallah Bou Habib dies
why: He served as foreign minister 2021-2025 and ambassador to Washington 1983-1990.

title: Franco-Lebanese arms dealer Ziad Takieddine dies
why: Central figure in the Sarkozy-Gaddafi financing case.

title: Online registration opens for expatriate voters in 2026 election
why: Platform ran to 20 November 2025; the election was later postponed.

title: Singer Fadel Shaker surrenders after twelve years in hiding
why: Wanted over the 2013 Sidon clashes; gave himself up in Ain al-Hilweh.

title: General Security says it foiled an Israeli bombing and assassination plot
why: Several arrests reported; Israel did not confirm.

title: Israeli jets strike Taybeh, Tayr Debba and three more towns
why: Marked a widening of the near-daily strikes during the ceasefire.

title: Army arrests Noah Zeiter, called Lebanon's most wanted drug trafficker
why: Raid in Baalbek.

title: Israel orders evacuation, then suspends strike at army's request
why: Rare case of the Lebanese army inspecting a target on request.

title: Former minister Amin Salam freed on bail in corruption probe
why: Released while investigated for falsification, embezzlement and blackmail of insurers; AP reports $100,000 bail.

title: Justice Ministry opinion: expatriates may vote for all 128 MPs
why: Non-binding view that sharpened the dispute over the six overseas seats before the election was postponed.

title: Israeli strikes on hotel and homes in Aramoun and Saadiyat kill 11
why: South of Beirut, in the first week of the 2026 war.

title: Cabinet bans IRGC activity and imposes visas on Iranians
why: Orders detention and deportation of Guards-linked individuals.

title: Parliament extends term to 31 May 2028 by 76 votes to 41
why: Four abstentions; elections due 1-10 May were cancelled and the expatriate-vote question left open.
dup_of: Parliament extends its term by two years

title: Israeli double-tap strike on Ramlet al-Baida seafront kills eight displaced people
why: Hit a beach used by displaced families in central Beirut.

title: Strike on Burj Qalaouiyah health centre kills 12 of its medical team
why: One of the deadliest single hits on health workers early in the war.

title: Overnight strikes on central Beirut kill at least 10 and wound dozens
why: Largely unannounced strikes, including Bachoura. Toll reports vary: Reuters at least 10, a preliminary Health Ministry count 12 killed and 41 wounded, Wikipedia six (corrected from '6 to 10').

title: Two Lebanese TV journalists killed in southern airstrike
why: Ali Shoeib (Al-Manar) and Fatima Ftouni (Al Mayadeen); Israel said Shoeib was a Radwan member, which his employer disputes.

title: Five paramedics killed in strike on Zawtar al-Gharbiyah
why: Part of repeated strikes on rescue crews recorded by WHO and MSF.

title: Strike in Ain Saade kills Lebanese Forces official Pierre Mouawad and wife
why: Hit a church-sponsored housing block; Israel said the target was a Hezbollah member. (other sources: 6 April)

title: Israel deploys a fifth division in south Lebanon
why: The 98th Division joined four others; Netanyahu said the US-Iran ceasefire excluded Lebanon.

title: Israeli strikes kill 357 on 8 April, within hours of the US-Iran truce
why: Health Ministry toll rose from 254 (initial civil defence count) to 357 killed and 1,223 wounded; Israel reported 100+ strikes within ten minutes (corrected from 'about 350 to 357' and 'Crisis Group counts at least 350', not verified).

title: Strike on Nabatieh kills 13 State Security personnel
why: Part of a wave that killed at least 28 that day.

title: Israeli forces encircle Bint Jbeil after days of ground combat
why: Town became the main ground battle of the war; the IDF said it killed over 100 fighters (Israeli claim).

title: Israel declares a 'yellow line' covering 55 southern villages
why: Residents barred from returning; zone wider than the area held at the 17 April truce.

title: Israeli soldier photographed smashing a Christ statue in Debel
why: Drew condemnation from Lebanese and Israeli leaders; Italian UNIFIL troops installed a new statue on 23 April.

title: Journalist Amal Khalil killed in strike at Tiri
why: Killed with a colleague wounded in a strike on a house in Tiri where they sheltered; rescue was obstructed by continued fire (CPJ, AP); sparked international outcry.

title: Constitutional Council rejects three appeals against the term extension
why: Unanimous 10-0; it added the two years should be shortened once the emergency ends.
dup_of: Constitutional Council unanimously rejects appeals against parliament's term extension

title: Israeli strikes kill over 40 a day on 1 and 2 May
why: Daily tolls peaked during the first truce, with new evacuation orders around Nabatieh.

title: Strikes on highway south of Beirut kill 22, including eight children
why: Cars hit on the Beirut-south road; images circulated by international media.

title: Strike on residential building in Sir el-Gharbiyeh kills 11
why: Six women and a child among the dead per Lebanese officials.

title: Parliament cancels 2026 official exams and suspends legal deadlines
why: Law 46/2026 suspends deadlines 1 March-31 July 2026; promulgated 27 July.

title: UNIFIL finds four tonnes of ammonium nitrate explosives at Houla
why: Peacekeepers neutralised explosives apparently left by Israeli forces.

title: Lawyers file complaint against banker who met Netanyahu
why: They cite Lebanese law barring contact with Israelis.

title: Lebanon arrests former Palestinian envoy on corruption charges
why: Charges relate to the Palestinian Authority.

title: About 15 Israelis cross into Lebanon and return after chase
why: IDF said mostly teenage girls slipped over the border.

title: Lebanon detains Assad-era general; decides to hand him to Syria
why: The former 17th Division commander was held over alleged wartime crimes; handover decided 18 August.

title: Parliament passes a contested general amnesty law
why: Passed a day after abolishing the death penalty.

title: Salam says hackers deleted posts condemning Israeli attacks
why: Cyber incident on official channels.

title: Aoun promulgates Law 71 amending the bank restructuring law
why: Amends Law 23 of 14 August 2025; follows parliament's August vote.

title: Hezbollah fires at Shebaa Farms; Israeli strikes kill nine
why: First Hezbollah fire after the ceasefire, called a warning response to violations; Israel replied with strikes.

title: Four Israeli reservists die in tunnel munitions blast at Labbouneh
why: Unmarked munitions detonated Hezbollah weapons; shows the unexploded-ordnance risk in the border zone.

title: Lebanon expels about 70 Syrian soldiers who entered illegally
why: Sent back via the Arida crossing weeks after Assad fell.

title: Hezbollah supporters block airport road; army uses tear gas, 23 soldiers hurt
why: Protest over the Mahan Air ban; 25 or more arrested over the attack on a UNIFIL convoy the day before.

title: US envoy Ortagus tells Beirut to disarm Hezbollah or face isolation
why: Visit with Aoun, Salam and Berri shortly after the new government formed.

title: Over 350 Alawite families flee Syrian coast into north Lebanon
why: Crossed the Nahr al-Kabir after the coastal violence; local communities took them in.

title: Israeli drone strike kills Hezbollah anti-tank commander Hassan Halawi
why: Struck at Qaaqaait al-Jisr during the ceasefire.

title: US envoy Barrack in Beirut; Aoun hands over Lebanese proposals
why: Hezbollah had called the US paper a capitulation on 5 July.

title: Aoun rules out normalisation with Israel, backs a 'no war' state
why: Says the state arms monopoly decision is irreversible.

title: Official source: no Syrian to keep 'displaced' status from January 2026
why: Reported plan; UNHCR said 205,000 had returned since December 2024.

title: Qassem rules out disarmament; Salam answers there is one government
why: Hezbollah's chief warned a confrontation would mean 'no life' for Lebanon; Salam rejected the civil-war threat.

title: Syrian foreign minister Shaibani visits Beirut
why: First high-level visit after Assad's fall: border, refugees, missing persons, detainees.

title: Israeli strike at Toul kills two; Israel names Hezbollah logistics chief Karaki
why: Part of the continued strikes in the south during the ceasefire.

title: Pope Leo XIV prays at Beirut port and celebrates Mass for 150,000
why: Closing day of his first trip abroad; he honoured victims of the 2020 blast.

title: Finance ministry orders tax declaration on Sayrafa trading profits
why: Taxpayers with over $15,000 in 2021-2023 transactions had to settle by 15 January 2026.

title: Reports say Riad Salameh case moves to highest criminal court
why: Follows his 2025 indictment and bail.

title: Israeli strikes in Baalbek area kill ten, including eight Hezbollah members
why: Eight days before the US-Israeli strikes on Iran; a separate Ain al-Hilweh strike killed two.

title: Israeli cabinet orders contact with Lebanon; Salam refuses Iran as go-between
why: Basis for the 14 April Washington talks.

title: Salam orders army to impose state authority and arms monopoly in Beirut
why: Issued the day after the 8 April strikes.

title: FATF keeps Lebanon on its grey list at June plenary
why: Two-year action plan runs to end-2026; listing began 25 October 2024.

title: Rome round ends; Israel-Lebanon talks to resume in October
why: Follows the 4 August opening; framework of 26 June still contested by Hezbollah.

title: Lebanon picks Alvarez & Marsal to audit central bank transactions 2019-2023
why: Covers 1 October 2019 to 31 December 2023.

title: Swiss parliament votes to ban Hezbollah
why: Federal Assembly vote 126-20 with 41 abstentions outlawing membership or support.

title: Palestinian factions hand arms to Lebanese army and vacate bases
why: Part of the state-arms-monopoly push right after the ceasefire.

title: Lebanon files UN Security Council complaint over ceasefire violations
why: One of several complaints lodged during the 60-day withdrawal window.

title: Lebanon approves extradition of Qaradawi's son to the UAE
why: Abdul Rahman Yusuf was detained on 28 December 2024 after returning from Syria.

title: Israeli drone strike in Tyre kills Radwan Force naval chief Haidar Hashem
why: Targeted killing during the ceasefire.

title: Army detains group, including Palestinians, over rocket launches at Israel
why: Hezbollah denied involvement in the two launches.

title: Israeli strikes hit Beirut suburbs without casualties
why: Another strike on the southern suburbs during the ceasefire.

title: Remains of Israeli soldier missing since 1982 returned from Syria
why: Zvi Feldman's body repatriated in a Mossad-IDF operation; links to the 1982 Lebanon war.

title: Israeli airstrike on Tripoli kills three
why: Rare strike in the north, far from the southern front.

title: Two soldiers die when Israeli drone explodes during inspection at Naqoura
why: Lebanese army said the drone crashed and blew up as troops inspected it.

title: Israeli strikes at Msayleh destroy bulldozers and cut a Beirut-south route
why: Hit reconstruction equipment; one killed, seven injured.

title: Israeli troops enter Blida and storm municipal hall, killing an employee
why: Aoun ordered the army to confront any Israeli incursion.

title: Israeli strikes kill three in south Lebanon, including a Quds Force member
why: Reported by Reuters and Al Jazeera.

title: Drone strike on vehicle at Majdal Anjar kills four Islamic Jihad operatives
why: Near the Syrian border in the Bekaa.

title: Israel seizes positions along the border and orders villages evacuated
why: The first ground moves after Hezbollah's 2 March attack; the full offensive began 16 March.

title: Israel orders evacuation of Dahieh; thousands flee
why: First full-suburb evacuation order of the 2026 war.

title: Macron pledges armoured vehicles and support to Lebanese army
why: Announced as France prepared a conference for the army.

title: Government says 1,039 killed since 2 March
why: Official count, three weeks into the war.

title: Iranian ambassador stays despite expulsion; Hezbollah ministers boycott cabinet
why: Order gave him until 29 March to leave; Hezbollah and allies opposed it.

title: US embassy tells Americans to leave Lebanon
why: Warning issued amid the expanding Israeli campaign.

title: Israeli chief of staff declares south of the Litani an operational zone
why: Zamir's statement preceded the fifth division and the 8 April strikes.

title: Government reports 1.2 million displaced
why: Lebanese government figure, in the sixth week of the war.

title: Iran closes Hormuz, citing Israeli attacks on Lebanon
why: Tehran said Lebanon was covered by the US-Iran truce.

title: EBRD plans EUR 5bn for Iran-war-hit economies including Lebanon
why: Also Egypt, Iraq and Jordan; focus on finance, firms and infrastructure.

title: Lebanese death toll in the war passes 2,000
why: Government figure; 2,167 killed and 7,061 injured by 15 April.

title: Aoun names former ambassador Simon Karam as negotiator
why: Karam led Lebanon's delegation at the 23 April Washington round.

title: France probes two Lebanese banks over billions moved despite capital controls
why: Naharnet report cited by Wikipedia's current events log.

title: Two Israeli soldiers jailed 30 days for smashing the Debel Christ statue
why: Military sentence after international outcry.

title: CRS: Israeli buffer zone covers about 5% of Lebanon's territory
why: Congressional Research Service note dated 20 July 2026: displaced over a million, killed over 4,300, buffer zone around 5% of Lebanon.

title: Netanyahu orders intensified strikes on Hezbollah
why: Issued weeks into the ceasefire; Ben-Gvir had called for large-scale combat.

title: Berri rejects 3 June deal; Aoun and Salam reject Iran's linkage
why: Berri wanted simultaneous Israeli and Hezbollah withdrawal south of the Litani.

title: France and Italy agree a multinational coalition for the post-UNIFIL period
why: Aims to support the Lebanese army after UNIFIL ends on 31 December 2026.

title: NNA: over 40,000 displaced have returned since the ceasefire
why: Figure reported by the National News Agency via L'Orient Today.

title: Netanyahu claims Christian villages asked for annexation; Marjayoun villages deny
why: Disputed claim about southern border villages.

title: CENTCOM delegation arrives in Beirut to implement the framework deal
why: Reported by the Financial Times; a US military team visited Beirut again on 11 July.

title: Israel's 401st Brigade ends eight-month deployment, claims 1,200 tunnels destroyed
why: Israeli claim reported by Israel National News and Jerusalem Post.

title: Israel frees four prisoners via the Red Cross, including two Syrians
why: Part of the effort to revive talks after Malek Ghazi's release on 3 September.

title: Army arrests Bashar al-Assad's cousin Suleiman al-Assad on drug charges
why: Held with two others in custody of the defence ministry.

title: Aoun makes first foreign trip as president, to Riyadh
why: First official Lebanese visit to Saudi Arabia in eight years; MBS and Aoun agreed to widen cooperation.

title: Cabinet issues 2025 state budget by decree
why: First budget of the Salam-Aoun era; parliament amended it on 30 June (decree 56 of 11 March per the parliament).

title: Cabinet cancels 2025 Brevet exams for Grade 9
why: Students get a school certificate by a new mechanism; the Brevet was cancelled again in 2026.

title: Aoun in Paris for first European visit; Macron condemns Beirut strike
why: Same day Israel struck Beirut's southern suburbs for the first time since the ceasefire; Cyprus and Greece joined a quadrilateral meeting.

title: Cabinet approves draft law on judicial independence
why: Half the Higher Judicial Council to be elected; parliament adopted a version on 31 July.

title: Cabinet removes North governor Ramzi Nohra after Tripoli election disputes
why: Tripoli's count was slow, with 140+ incidents and calls from LADE to rerun the vote.

title: Palestinian camp weapons collection postponed because of the Iran-Israel war
why: Scheduled start in Beirut camps delayed hours before it began; Abbas-Aoun deal of 21 May stood.

title: Army closes smuggling routes at Masharih al-Qaa on the Syrian border
why: Government counts 136 illegal crossings on the roughly 375 km border, over half in the Bekaa.

title: Army receives PLO heavy weapons from six of twelve camps
why: Covers Shatila, Mar Elias, Burj al-Barajneh and four southern camps; Hamas and Islamic Jihad excluded.

title: UN: about 200,000 Syrians returned home this year; Lebanon offers $100 plan
why: Lebanon's plan gives $100 and fine exemptions to those who pledge not to return as asylum seekers.

title: Ain al-Hilweh and Beddawi camps hand over weapons to the army
why: Five truckloads from Ain al-Hilweh and three from Beddawi, as part of the state arms monopoly drive.

title: Aoun and Sharaa meet at Doha summit, call it a turning point
why: Talked border demarcation and refugee returns; detainees left to the judiciary.

title: PLO hands over fifth batch of heavy weapons at Ain al-Hilweh
why: Palestinian camp handovers began in August; about 222,000 Palestinian refugees live in Lebanon per UNRWA.

title: Winter storm floods Nahr el-Kabir area; informal settlements submerged
why: UNHCR reports Semmaqiye settlements flooded on 12-13 January, about 1,200 people relocated; 3,600 people affected by end-January.

title: IMF mission ends; central bank says $8.1bn returns to depositors by end-2026
why: Souaid cites Circulars 158 and 166; Berri says any law must protect all deposits.

title: Israeli strikes on Talousa and Haris kill at least eleven
why: First major exchange of fire after the 27 November ceasefire.

title: World Bank damage assessment: $11bn reconstruction needs, $3-5bn public
why: Covers 8 October 2023-20 December 2024; $6-8bn expected from private financing, mainly housing and commerce.
dup_of: World Bank puts reconstruction needs at $11bn

title: Iran's Araghchi says disarmament will fail; Beirut summons Iranian ambassador
why: Reaction to the 7 August cabinet decision; lawmakers called it interference and urged a UN complaint.

title: Lebanese forces exchange fire with smugglers on the northern Bekaa border
why: Cited by Crisis Group as proof of insecurity on the Syria border.

title: Israeli strike wounds four Electricity of Lebanon workers in Nabatieh
why: One of several strikes on civil infrastructure staff during the ceasefire.

title: World Bank: 2025 growth 3.5%, forecasts 4% for 2026 before the war
why: Winter monitor 'A Fragile Rebound' also saw inflation at 15.2% in 2025 and single digits in 2026.

title: UNESCO inscribes the castles of Mount Amel on the World Heritage List
why: Listed despite Israeli opposition, two days after Tyre went on the Danger list. Corrects: this is the main List.
dup_of: Mount Amel Castles inscribed as World Heritage in Danger

title: World Bank: 2025 growth revised to 4.2%; 2026 forecast contraction 6.4%
why: Summer monitor: 2025 surplus 3.9% of GDP, 2026 inflation seen at 17.5%, debt restructuring talks yet to begin.

title: Salam presents 'Reform and Rescue' ministerial statement to parliament
why: Promised an IMF programme, independent regulators and airport and port upgrades; confidence vote followed on 26 February.

title: US envoy Barrack makes first visit to Beirut
why: Began a series of visits that produced the July proposal on Hezbollah's arms.

title: Cabinet passes gap bill 13 to 9; $100,000 back over four years
why: Those under $100,000 are 85% of depositors; Berri opposed it; the bill went to parliament.
dup_of: Cabinet approves financial gap draft law
